candidates.attributionBasis: The passage is an uninterrupted continuation of Jimmy Akin's moderator-introduced conclusion and articulates his previously proposed evaluative standard.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The proposed cumulative method supplies the operative test by which corroborated Gospel claims and alleged mistakes are to be weighed against each other.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Ehrman's reliance on selected contradictions and historically doubtful narratives to support a general verdict of Gospel unreliability.

candidates.contextSummary: Because every Gospel claim cannot be independently checked, Akin proposes assessing broad corroboration across major, intermediate, and lesser claims while accounting for ancient conventions.

candidates.speaker: Jimmy Akin
candidates.proposition: Differences produced by approximate gist reporting are not errors merely because one account gives a different level of precision from another.
candidates.attributionBasis: This remains within Jimmy Akin's continuous closing statement and develops his expressly introduced discussion of ancient approximating practices.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The argument directly answers contradiction claims by distinguishing genuine factual incompatibility from variation expected when ancient authors convey an event's essence.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Ehrman's position that divergent Gospel details reveal authorial changes and historical contradictions rather than permissible reporting variation.

candidates.contextSummary: Akin illustrates that two descriptions may both be correct at different precisional levels and warns against reading gist accounts as exact transcripts.

candidates.speaker: Jimmy Akin
candidates.proposition: Even granting or expanding the alleged errors, the many Gospel claims conceded or shown probable outweigh them, so unreliability has not been established.
candidates.attributionBasis: The passage completes Jimmy Akin's uninterrupted concluding statement and explicitly weighs Bart Ehrman's allegations against the evening's broader record.
candidates.loadBearingReason: This is the pro side's final cumulative inference on the resolution: the alleged errors are insufficient to overcome corroborated and conceded historical content.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Ehrman's overall contention that the examples of contradiction, invention, and alteration justify classifying the canonical Gospels as historically unreliable.

candidates.contextSummary: Akin provisionally grants the cited problems, even allows their number to be increased, and concludes that they still fail to counterbalance the accounts' supported claims.
